content: This schedule outlines vaccination recommendations effective as of January 1, 2016. Any missed doses should be administered at a subsequent visit when appropriate and feasible. Combination vaccines are generally preferred over separate injections of equivalent component vaccines. Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) Vaccine Routine Vaccination: Administer a 2or 3-dose primary series and a booster dose (dose 3 or 4, depending on the vaccine used in the primary series) at 12–15 months of age to complete the full Hib vaccine series. For ActHIB, MenHibrix, or Pentacel, the primary series consists of 3 doses at 2, 4, and 6 months of age. For PedvaxHIB or COMVAX, the primary series consists of 2 doses at 2 and 4 months of age; a dose at 6 months is not indicated. A single booster dose (dose 3 or 4) of any Hib vaccine should be administered at 12–15 months of age. Hib vaccine is not routinely recommended for patients aged 5 years or older, except for certain high-risk groups. Catch-Up Vaccination: If dose 1 was administered at 12–14 months, administer a second (final) dose at least 8 weeks after dose 1. If both doses were PRP-OMP (PedvaxHIB or COMVAX) and administered before the first birthday, administer a third (final) dose at 12–59 months and at least 8 weeks after the second dose. If the first dose was administered at 7–11 months, administer the second dose at least 4 weeks later and a third (final) dose at 12–15 months or 8 weeks after the second dose, whichever is later. For unvaccinated children aged 15 months or older, administer only 1 dose. High-Risk Conditions: Children aged 12–59 months at increased risk for Hib disease (e.g., chemotherapy recipients, those with asplenia, HIV infection, or complement deficiency) who received no doses or only 1 dose of Hib vaccine before 12 months of age should receive 2 additional doses 8 weeks apart. Children who received 2 or more doses of Hib vaccine before 12 months of age should receive 1 additional dose. Patients younger than 5 years undergoing chemotherapy or radiation who received a Hib vaccine dose(s) within 14 days of starting therapy or during therapy should repeat the dose(s) at least 3 months after therapy completion. Hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) recipients should be revaccinated with a 3-dose regimen of Hib vaccine starting 6–12 months after successful transplant, regardless of vaccination history, with doses administered at least 4 weeks apart. A single dose of any Hib-containing vaccine should be administered to unimmunized children and adolescents aged 15 months or older undergoing elective splenectomy, ideally at least 14 days before the procedure. Hepatitis B (HepB) Vaccine Routine Vaccination: Administer monovalent HepB vaccine to all newborns before hospital discharge. If the mother’s HBsAg status is unknown, administer HepB vaccine within 12 hours of birth regardless of birth weight. For infants weighing <2,000 grams, also administer hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours of birth. Determine the mother’s HBsAg status as soon as possible. Doses Following the Birth Dose: Administer the second dose at age 1–2 months. Monovalent HepB vaccine should be used for doses administered before age 6 weeks. Infants who did not receive a birth dose should receive 3 doses of a HepB-containing vaccine on a schedule of 0, 1–2 months, and 6 months, starting as soon as feasible. Administer the second dose 1–2 months after the first dose (minimum interval of 4 weeks). Administer the third dose at least 8 weeks after the second dose AND at least 16 weeks after the first dose. The final dose should be administered no earlier than age 24 weeks. Catch-Up Vaccination: Unvaccinated persons should complete a 3-dose series. A 2-dose series (doses separated by at least 4 months) of adult formulation Recombivax HB is licensed for use in children aged 11–15 years. Rotavirus (RV) Vaccines Routine Vaccination: If Rotarix is used, administer a 2-dose series at 2 and 4 months of age. If RotaTeq is used, administer a 3-dose series at ages 2, 4, and 6 months. If any dose in the series was RotaTeq or the vaccine product is unknown, administer a total of 3 doses of RV vaccine. Catch-Up Vaccination: The maximum age for the first dose in the series is 14 weeks, 6 days; vaccination should not be initiated for infants aged 15 weeks, 0 days or older. The maximum age for the final dose in the series is 8 months, 0 days. Pneumococcal Vaccines Routine Vaccination with PCV13: Administer a 4-dose series of PCV13 vaccine at ages 2, 4, 6 months, and 12–15 months. Catch-Up Vaccination with PCV13: Administer 1 dose of PCV13 to all healthy children aged 24–59 months who are not completely vaccinated for their age. High-Risk Conditions: Administer all recommended PCV13 doses prior to PPSV23 vaccination if possible. For children aged 2–5 years with conditions such as chronic heart disease, chronic lung disease, diabetes, asplenia, or immunodeficiency, administer 1 dose of PCV13 if an incomplete schedule of 3 doses of PCV (PCV7 and/or PCV13) was received previously. Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine (IPV) Routine Vaccination: Administer a 4-dose series of IPV at ages 2, 4, 6–18 months, and 4–6 years. The final dose should be administered on or after the fourth birthday and at least 6 months after the previous dose. Catch-Up Vaccination: If 4 or more doses are administered before age 4 years, an additional dose should be administered at age 4–6 years and at least 6 months after the previous dose. Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) Vaccine Routine Vaccination: Administer a 2-dose series of MMR vaccine at ages 12–15 months and 4–6 years. Catch-Up Vaccination: Ensure all school-aged children and adolescents have had 2 doses of MMR vaccine, with a minimum interval of 4 weeks between doses. Varicella (VAR) Vaccine Routine Vaccination: Administer a 2-dose series of VAR vaccine at ages 12–15 months and 4–6 years. Catch-Up Vaccination: Ensure all persons aged 7–18 years without evidence of immunity have 2 doses of varicella vaccine. Hepatitis A (HepA) Vaccine Routine Vaccination: Initiate the 2-dose HepA vaccine series at 12–23 months, with doses separated by 6–18 months. Catch-Up Vaccination: Administer 2 doses of HepA vaccine separated by at least 6 months to unvaccinated persons aged 2 years and older. This detailed guidance ensures that all children and adolescents receive appropriate immunizations based on their age, health status, and risk factors.
